subject: Pricing follow-up: token benchmarking vs OpenAI/Anthropic
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Cooper <jane.cooper@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing follow-up: token benchmarking vs OpenAI/Anthropic

Hi Jane — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and a couple of follow-ups so we can run a tailored pricing comparison: 

Summary from our call:
- Primary workload: customer support summarization + long-form generation for help center articles.
- Expected peak qps: ~40 requests/s; average request ~1.8k tokens (prompt+response).
- Current hosting: mix of OpenAI for chat and a hosted open-model for bulk embeddings.
- Key asks: target $/1M tokens, budget range for next 12 months, procurement contact and timing.

What we need to finalize pricing: 
1) Monthly token volume (or ballpark monthly range) — this will drive reserved vs on-demand economics.
2) Target $/1M tokens you're expecting (if you have a benchmark vs OpenAI/Anthropic).
3) Any compliance/contract requirements (SOC2, data residency).

Preliminary note: I attached a short pricing comparison (Redwood vs OpenAI/Anthropic vs common open-model hosts) — see the spreadsheet. Our initial hypothesis based on the numbers you gave on the call is that with committed volume (>=100M tokens/mo) we should be able to get to a competitive $/1M token target vs hosted OpenAI rates while keeping lower tail latency and better isolation than public host tiers.

Next steps I propose:
- You share monthly token range + target $/1M (quick reply is fine).
- I'll return a 2-tier pricing quote (on-demand + 12-mo reserved) with explicit unit economics and example monthly invoices.
- If that looks good, we'll pull in legal/procurement and draft an initial MSA + SOW.

Thanks — I'm around next week for a 30-min pricing walk-through if you want to run through the spreadsheet together.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: Redwood_Token_Pricing_Comparison.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Jane Cooper <jane.cooper@acme.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@acme.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 09:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up: token benchmarking vs OpenAI/Anthropic

Vanessa — thanks for the summary and for the spreadsheet. Quick answers below: 

Monthly volume (estimates):
- Pilot (next 3 months): 8M – 12M tokens/mo
- Q4 target: 60M – 120M tokens/mo depending on retention and feature rollout

Budget / target $/1M tokens:
- Our procurement target for production is in the $15k – $30k range per 1M tokens (that's what our finance pulled as an acceptable unit cost when compared to self-hosted open-model hosts).
- For context, current line items we see in market: OpenAI averages we've been quoted (for chat mix) are ~ $45k – $70k per 1M tokens depending on model; Anthropic quotes often sit a bit lower around $35k – $55k; pure open-model hosts (with less SLA) can be as low as $8k – $18k.

Compliance: SOC2 Type 2 is required; data residency in us-east preferred.

Procurement lead: Tom Hsu (cc'd) — timeline: procurement expects to review all commercial terms in July and, if pricing works, target signing in early August.

Tom — if you need any more detailed volume forecasts or a procurement questionnaire, let us know.

Thanks,
Jane
Head of Product, Acme AI

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Cooper <jane.cooper@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@acme.ai>
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 11:56:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up: token benchmarking vs OpenAI/Anthropic

Jane / Tom — great, this is super helpful. A few notes and an explicit pricing sketch based on the ranges you shared: 

1) Benchmark framing (from our market work):
- OpenAI (hosted chat/completion tiers): typically priced at a premium for the closed models; you'll see higher $/1M for higher-capability models (your numbers match what customers report).
- Anthropic: generally slightly cheaper than OpenAI for comparable chat workloads, but still premium vs self-hosted open-models.
- Hosted open-model vendors: lower $/1M for on-demand, but often tradeoffs: higher p50/p95 latency, less predictable tail latency, and fewer enterprise-grade SLAs.

2) Redwood price sketch (ballpark, assumes SOC2 + us-east residency):
- On-demand: $38k / 1M tokens (no commit) — aimed to be immediately competitive with Anthropic for baseline latency and reliability.
- Committed (12-mo, 3-tier usage):
  - Tier A: 10M–50M tokens/mo => $26k / 1M tokens
  - Tier B: 50M–150M tokens/mo => $18k / 1M tokens
  - Tier C: >150M tokens/mo => $12k / 1M tokens
- Reserved capacity add-on (dedicated GPUs, SLA-backed): additional monthly fee, which reduces effective $/1M further by ~20% depending on utilization.

Notes on assumptions: these are preliminary — final numbers will depend on exact request size distribution (your 1.8k avg is very helpful), prefix caching opportunities, and whether you need KV-caching across conversations. I've attached a worked example in the spreadsheet showing effective monthly invoice at 60M tokens/mo for on-demand vs committed.

3) Next steps (proposed):
- I'll update the attached Mutual Action Plan with the July procurement window and proposed procurement kickoff (week of July 6).
- If you want, we can schedule a 30-min pricing deep-dive with our solutions engineer to walk the spreadsheet and assumptions (recommended for wire-level unit economics).
- I'll also loop in Legal/Partner Ops once you confirm that the $18k / 1M target (Tier B) is within range you can present to procurement.

Can you confirm whether the Tier B target ($18k / 1M) is realistic for Acme as a negotiation anchor? If not, share a counter target and we'll iterate.

Thanks — cc'ing Marissa (our AE lead) on procurement logistics.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Mutual_Action_Plan.docx

From: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@acme.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Jane Cooper <jane.cooper@acme.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up: token benchmarking vs OpenAI/Anthropic

Vanessa — thanks for the clear options. We reviewed the Tier B anchor with finance and operations. Quick response:

- Tier B ($18k / 1M) is within range to present, but procurement will ask for a firm committed quote closer to $15k / 1M for 12-mo with a 6–12 week implementation SLA.
- We'd be amenable to a hybrid: 12-mo commit at $16k / 1M with a reserved capacity add-on to bring the effective price down further if utilization >80%.
- Please put together a short commercial term sheet (pricing + deployment SLA + SOC2 confirmation) and we'll route to procurement next week.

Schedule: procurement kickoff week of July 6 looks right.

Tom Hsu
Head of Procurement, Acme AI
